mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best compares the inertia of motion of a moving object with the inertia of rest of a stationary object?

options.A: A moving object tends to continue moving at a constant velocity, while a stationary object tends to remain at rest.
options.B: A moving object tends to speed up over time, whereas a stationary object tends to stay still.
options.C: Both moving and stationary objects will eventually come to rest without external forces.
options.D: A stationary object will start moving on its own, while a moving object will stop.

mcqs.answer: A moving object tends to continue moving at a constant velocity, while a stationary object tends to remain at rest.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion refers to an object's resistance to any change in its velocity (both speed and direction). Hence a moving object keeps moving at constant velocity unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. Inertia of rest is the analogous resistance of a stationary object to start moving. Option A captures this contrast correctly; the other options either describe acceleration, assume spontaneous motion, or ignore the role of external forces.

mcqs.question: A car traveling straight on a highway suddenly encounters a sharp turn. According to Newton's first law, which statement correctly describes the car's inertia of direction?

options.A: The car will instantly change direction to follow the turn because of its inertia of direction.
options.B: The car tends to continue moving straight ahead, resisting the change in direction.
options.C: The car will stop moving when it reaches the turn due to inertia of direction.
options.D: Inertia of direction causes the car to accelerate while turning.

mcqs.answer: The car tends to continue moving straight ahead, resisting the change in direction.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law states that an object in motion maintains its state of motion, which includes both speed and direction, unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force. Therefore, the car naturally wants to keep moving straight; a lateral force (friction from the road, steering) is required to change its direction. Option B reflects this; the other options misinterpret inertia as causing immediate direction change, stopping, or acceleration.

mcqs.question: Newton's first law of motion states that:

options.A: An object will accelerate if a net force acts on it.
options.B: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.D: Every object moves in a circle unless a force stops it.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: This is the exact wording of Newton's first law, also called the law of inertia. It emphasizes that both the state of rest and uniform straight‑line motion persist without a net external force. Option A describes Newton's second law, while C and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example that illustrates Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: A book lying undisturbed on a table.
options.B: A ball rolling down a slope accelerating.
options.C: A car speeding up when the driver presses the accelerator.
options.D: A rocket lifting off from the launch pad.

mcqs.answer: A book lying undisturbed on a table.
mcqs.explanation: The book remains at rest because the forces acting on it (gravity and normal reaction) are balanced, demonstrating inertia of rest. Options B, C, and D involve unbalanced forces causing acceleration, which relate to Newton's second law rather than the first.

mcqs.question: Inertia is best defined as:

options.A: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of motion.
options.B: The force that causes objects to move.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is a property of matter that quantifies resistance to changes in velocity (including direction). It is not a force, nor is it equivalent to weight (which depends on gravity) or speed. Option A captures the correct definition.

mcqs.question: A soccer ball is placed on a flat field and remains motionless until a player kicks it. Which principle explains this behavior?
mcqs.explanation: The ball stays at rest because, in the absence of an unbalanced external force, an object at rest tends to remain at rest—this is inertia of rest, a direct consequence of Newton's first law. Newton's third law concerns action-reaction pairs, while conservation of energy and gravity are unrelated to the ball's initial state.

mcqs.question: Which scenario best illustrates the inertia of motion?

options.A: A book sliding down a frictionless incline and speeding up.
options.B: A hockey puck sliding on ice continues to glide at constant speed after being struck, assuming negligible friction.
options.C: A car coming to a stop at a red light.
options.D: A ball thrown upward that slows down and falls back.

mcqs.answer: A hockey puck sliding on ice continues to glide at constant speed after being struck, assuming negligible friction.
mcqs.explanation: The puck maintains its state of uniform motion because there is little external unbalanced force (friction) acting on it, exemplifying inertia of motion. Option A involves acceleration, C involves deceleration, and D involves a change in direction due to gravity, all of which are not pure demonstrations of inertia of motion.

mcqs.question: A cyclist moving north at constant speed suddenly hits a patch of oil and begins to slide eastward. According to Newton's first law, which statement is correct?

options.A: The cyclist would have continued moving north because inertia of direction resists any change in direction.
options.B: The cyclist will immediately turn east because inertia of direction forces a change.
options.C: The cyclist will stop moving due to inertia of rest.
options.D: The cyclist's speed will increase because of inertia of motion.

mcqs.answer: The cyclist would have continued moving north because inertia of direction resists any change in direction.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law states that an object maintains both its speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force. The oil provides a lateral force that changes the cyclist's direction to east; without that force, the cyclist would have kept moving north. Options B, C, and D misinterpret the role of inertia.
